scope: available bitmap to fake AndroidActionExecutor; no OS capture, gesture injection or game response
limitations: Production dispatcher layout is reproduced: QuickJS on Default and serialized Android operations on the dedicated resource thread.
Fixed available bitmap and fake gesture boundary; no MediaProjection, actual Android gestures or game response.
Diagnostic recording is measured, but no viewer is attached; UI rendering cost is not included.
CPU includes warmup, runtime validation/setup, legacy state initialization and benchmark instrumentation.
Heap/PSS are snapshots of the test process, including fixtures, models, tracing instrumentation and GC variation; they are not per-operation allocations or physical-device app measurements.
This collection retains the initial three-warmup/twenty-sample protocol; the cold early rounds show substantial variation.
Host timings include host work and response serialization; JS parsing and dispatcher traversal remain in total reaction time.
